Liubavas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marijampolė County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Liubavas's Jewish community, established in the second half of the 18th century, numbered just 54 people across four households as early as 1765. In the early years of Lithuanian independence, a secular Jewish community here was organized with guidance from the Ministry of Jewish Affairs in Kaunas — part of the new state's formal recognition of Jewish communal autonomy. The town was the birthplace of Ephraim Greenberg, editor of the Kaunas daily Dos Vort and a Socialist Zionist party official; Rabbi Elchanan Rosenholtz was among those murdered here in 1941.
